name: Belmont
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Belmont, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Belmont, MA: a flashlight Candy Cane Hunt, family gingerbread night, Turn On The Town in Belmont Center and Santa on a fire engine.
lede: Belmont keeps its Christmas close to home: Santa greeting children from a Belmont fire engine in Belmont Center, a flashlight candy cane hunt for little ones and a family gingerbread night at the Beech Street Center.
celebrates: Belmont's season starts in Belmont Center with Turn On The Town, the Belmont Center Business Association's tree lighting, when Leonard Street closes to traffic for an evening of music, treats and Santa. The Belmont Voice counted more than a thousand people at one recent lighting, with Santa and Mrs. Claus greeting kids from atop a Belmont fire engine and free fried dough and cupcakes for the crowd. Belmont Recreation adds smaller programs at the Beech Street Center on Beech Street: a flashlight Candy Cane Hunt for children up to age 10 and a gingerbread house night for the whole family, both with cocoa and cookie decorating.
lastyear: In 2025 Turn On The Town took place on Thursday, December 4, from 6 to 8 pm along Leonard Street in Belmont Center. The Belmontonian reported that the town's Christmas tree beside Bellmont Cafe would be switched on at about 6:15 pm, and pictures with Santa were offered outside Cambridge Savings Bank from 6:30 to 8 pm. The Belmont Voice later covered the night under the headline Belmont Celebrates 2025 Turn On The Town.
facts: Belmont was incorporated on March 18, 1859, from land that had belonged to Watertown, Waltham and West Cambridge, the town now called Arlington. The town history page traces settlement in the area back to 1630, when Sir Richard Saltonstall arrived with about 40 families. Belmont took its name from Bellmont, the estate of John Perkins Cushing, the largest donor to its creation, and Cushing Square still carries his name today.
trains: Belmont has two stops on the MBTA Fitchburg Line, Belmont in Belmont Center and Waverley, and inbound trains reach North Station after a single stop at Porter in Cambridge. That makes a commuter rail ride into Boston an easy add-on to a holiday day out. For a train ride with Christmas lights, Edaville in Carver runs a holiday train, and the Boston Street Railway Association preserves the region's streetcar and trolley history.

kidfact: Belmont is named after a big estate called Bellmont that belonged to John Perkins Cushing. He gave more money than anyone else to help start the town in 1859, and Cushing Square is named after him.
faq: When is Turn On The Town in Belmont?

Turn On The Town is held on a Thursday evening in early December along Leonard Street in Belmont Center. In 2025 it ran on December 4 from 6 to 8 pm, with the tree beside Bellmont Cafe lit at about 6:15 pm and pictures with Santa outside Cambridge Savings Bank. Check the Belmont Center Business Association events page for this year's details.
Where can kids see Santa in Belmont?

The best-known Santa visit is at Turn On The Town in Belmont Center, where Santa and Mrs. Claus have greeted children from atop a Belmont fire engine and posed for pictures outside Cambridge Savings Bank. Belmont Recreation's Candy Cane Hunt at the Beech Street Center also promises a Special Guest.
What holiday programs does Belmont Recreation run for kids?

Belmont Recreation lists a flashlight Candy Cane Hunt for ages 1 to 10 and a family Gingerbread House Decorating night, both at the Beech Street Center at 266 Beech Street. Both programs need registration through Belmont Recreation's online catalog, and both include cookie decorating for children.
Can we take the train to Belmont?

Yes. The MBTA Fitchburg Line stops at Belmont, in Belmont Center, and at Waverley. Inbound trains make one stop at Porter in Cambridge before reaching North Station in Boston, so Belmont Center's holiday events are a short ride from the city.
